absent: No participatory or action research, no Santos, no African-continental education scholarship, and no empirical education research; the Dutch and European vocational context is naturally outside its frame.
forYou: Wynter, Mignolo and Táíwò here overlap with your decolonial line, but the Fals-Borda and Santos strands you work from are absent — the argument runs through US Black studies rather than Latin American participatory thought.
method: References from the paper; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in that list.
narrative: The deep root is Caribbean anticolonial thought: Fanon (1963, 2008), C.L.R. James (1989), Glissant (1992) and above all Sylvia Wynter (1976, 2003) on the coloniality of being.

Onto that the paper grafts US Afro-pessimism — Wilderson (2003, 2010, 2017) and Hartman (2007) — as its account of why emancipation did not produce full membership. The positive half comes from Afrofuturism, from Dery's coinage (1994) through Eshun (2003) and Kilgore (2014).

Reparations enter through Táíwò (2022), whose 'constructive view' the authors treat as the one that fits a futures orientation. Method is represented by a single source, Collier (2011) on process tracing.
